children: Macquarie has initiated coverage on National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) stock with an ‘Outperform’ rating and a target price of Rs 1,965 per share, just ahead of NSE shares’ listing today following the country's second-largest IPO.

The brokerage described NSE as “The Dominator”, citing its leading market share, comprehensive suite of services, technology infrastructure and deep liquidity. Macquarie said these attributes make NSE a lynchpin of India's ongoing financialisation. “Entrenched network effects, industry-leading profitability and cash” underpin the brokerage's positive outlook on the exchange, Macquarie said.
Rs 1,965 target price on NSE stock

implies an upside of about 10 percent over the IPO issue price of Rs 1,785 per share. NSE shares are scheduled to list on the BSE at 10 am on Thursday. The stock cannot list on its own exchange under regulatory rules governing recognised stock exchanges.

The NSE IPO, which was entirely an offer for sale by existing shareholders, raised about Rs 22,569 crore and was subscribed 5.71 times. Investors bid for 50.58 crore shares against 8.86 crore shares on offer, generating demand of nearly Rs 90,300 crore.

At the upper end of its Rs 1,700-1,785 price band, NSE was valued at roughly 43 times FY26 earnings. The IPO was India's second-largest public issue, behind Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870-crore offering in 2024 and ahead of LIC's Rs 21,000-crore IPO in 2022.
NSE's listing comes as Macquarie takes a positive view of India's broader exchange ecosystem, initiating coverage on both BSE and Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) with ‘Outperform’ ratings.

Macquarie initiated coverage on BSE stock with an ‘Outperform’ rating and a target price of Rs 4,000 per share, describing India's oldest stock exchange as “The Challenger”. The target price implies an upside of over 22 percent. The brokerage added that the optionality across BSE's platform prompts its positive outlook on the exchange.

Macquarie said BSE's pivot towards index options has made it a credible competitor to NSE. Its expanding platform and market-share gains provide scope for further revenue and margin expansion, while earnings growth and improving margins should support strong cash generation, it said.

Macquarie also initiated coverage on MCX with an ‘Outperform’ rating and a target price of Rs 3,820 per share, calling the commodity exchange “The Phoenix” after its recovery from what the brokerage described as near-death conditions to establish a dominant position in commodity trading.

The brokerage said MCX's first-mover advantage has helped it build a strong market position, while relatively low penetration across investors and products provides a long runway for growth. Despite a high FY26 base, Macquarie expects expansion in products and investor participation to support visible growth and high margins.

title: NSE IPO: Macquarie starts coverage with Outperform, sees NSE as ‘The Dominator’; bullish on BSE, MCX too
